page.monCommandsFootnote: All commands support --json for scripts and agent workflows

monFeatures.title: Health across every target, one command
monFeatures.detail: health runs HTTP or TCP probes against every target defined in deploy.yaml. Pass or fail per service, with latency.

monFeatures.title: Running state, uptime, and image SHA
monFeatures.detail: status gives you the three things you always want during an incident — current state, how long it's been that way, and exactly what's running.

monFeatures.title: Remote logs without SSH sessions
monFeatures.detail: logs streams docker logs from the host. --lines for a tail, --follow for live tail. No more SSH into a box just to tail a file.

page.monConfigLead2: Deploy and observability are paired by design. If kb-deploy knows about a target, kb-monitor does too.
page.monCtaTitle: Set up once. Forget about monitoring.
page.monHeroTitle: Set it up once. Let the
page.monHeroDescription: kb-monitor observes services deployed by kb-deploy. Every command has --json with a stable schema — the agent runs health checks, reads logs, and reacts autonomously.

monCommands.desc: Run health probes against every target. Pass or fail per service, with response latency.
Probe a specific target. Useful for post-deploy verification in CI or agent workflows.
Running state, uptime, and image SHA for every target. The three things you need during an incident.
Structured output for agents and dashboards. Stable schema, every field documented.
Fetch the last 100 lines of logs for a target. No SSH session, no docker ps needed.
Stream live logs for a target from your laptop. Ctrl-C to stop, no cleanup needed.
Execute a command inside the running container. Any command after -- is passed through verbatim.

page.monConfigLead1: kb-monitor reads .kb/deploy.yaml — the same file used to deploy services. No second source of truth, no parallel inventory.
page.monMetaDesc: Agent-native service observability. Health, uptime, image SHA, logs, exec — all with --json.
